newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish president to see Yilmaz in govt search.
newsitem.headline: Turkish president to see Yilmaz in govt search.

text.p: Turkish President Suleyman Demirel invited opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz to his residence on Friday amid the search for a new prime minister to succeed Islamist Necmettin Erbakan.
Anatolian news agency said Demirel would hold talks with Yilmaz at 5 p.m. (1400 GMT). It gave no more details of the meeting, the second between the pair in two days.
Yilmaz is one of the favourites to be appointed as prime minister-designate by Demirel but he lacks a clear majority to get a confidence vote through parliament.
Conservative Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller, a bitter rival of Yilmaz, is also in the running for the top job.
Istanbul shares jumped on hopes that Demirel would give Yilmaz the nod. The general index was up 2.25 percent by early afternoon.
Yilmaz's Motherland Party (ANAP) said it was ready to rule.
"Hope for a new start for the country has been born," party spokesman Cumhur Ersumer told a news conference. "ANAP is ready to take over the duties of the administration," he said.
Erbakan, NATO member Turkey's first Islamist leader, resigned on Wednesday after months of pressure from the secularist military.
He asked Demirel to approve a plan under which Ciller would head a new coalition with the Islamists to take Turkey to early elections by next spring at the latest.
Turkish media said the president did not favour Ciller, Islamist Erbakan's ally in an "odd couple" coalition since last June.
Yilmaz, prime minister twice since 1991, was confident he could head a government that would get past a parliamentary vote of confidence.
"There is an extremely high possibility that a government formed under me can win a vote of confidence," he told the NTV television news channel late on Thursday night.
